- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows lagged reaction to sentiment: if sentiment turns bullish after 3–5 days, model doesn’t catch it until 7–10 days later; apply 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven moves.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day prices instead of linear extrapolation.
